note: FIGURES tools/check-figure-light.mjs FINDS BRIGHTER THAN THEIR NIGHT, NOT YET RULED ON (errata 205). Each was measured when the check was written: the figure's mean drawn luminance against Thad's at its feet, in the same grade and lamp tint, over the limit there (1.12, raised inside a lamp's pool). Nothing was changed: each is for Tyler to look at beside Thad (python3 tools/art/beside-thad.py <id> <out.png>) and rule on. The check prints every entry on every run, fails on a figure flagged and not listed here, and fails on an entry that is no longer flagged -- take it out when it is fixed or ruled fine. The check cannot tell a white apron from a bright lamp; `why` says which this looks like.

known.fix: Grade him into the room: a `figureLight` in reference/room-39/annotation.json naming bakehouse_boy, brightness about 0.68, a little warm; or declare the open door's light if it is meant to fall on him.

known.why: His frame carries the ironing board and its white sheet, which is most of the excess: his own dark green jacket is about Thad's level. The laundry declares no lamp, so nothing in the room's data lights the sheet.
known.fix: Either grade him (a `figureLight` in reference/room-28/annotation.json naming sheng, brightness about 0.72) or, if the stove's fire is meant to light the sheet, declare it as a lamp in the laundry's annotation so the room says so.

known.why: The man in the white shirt and hat at the claim markers, in the dark of the row with no lamp near: his shirt sleeves and face are lighter than Thad's, and boundary_a beside him measures 0.96.
known.fix: A `figureLight` in reference/room-27/annotation.json naming boundary_b, brightness about 0.92, so he matches boundary_a.

known.why: By the swinging doors in his white shirt sleeves, at the edge of the stove's pool. The Nugget's `figureLight` grades Thad and Deke warmer and darker (Tyler, 2026-11-01) but not the fiddler, so he is drawn in his generation's own light beside a graded Thad. Only just over.
